title: Greatest Common Divisor
statement:
Find the largest number that divides both of two non-negative
integers.

## Your function

```
int gcd(int a, int b);
```

Both arguments are zero or positive and fit in an `int`.

## Watch out

- `gcd(0, n)` is `n`, and `gcd(0, 0)` is `0`. Every number divides zero.
- Euclid's algorithm is three lines: while `b` is not zero, replace the pair
  `(a, b)` with `(b, a % b)`. Trying every divisor from the smaller number
  downwards also works, and is dramatically slower.
- `%` on two non-negative `int`s is well behaved, so no sign juggling is
  needed here.

tests.name: both zero
tests.description: Nothing divides into a largest common factor here, and 0 is the conventional answer.

tests.name: zero and a number
tests.description: Every number divides 0, so the answer is the other one.
